neet_che_u18_t02_1.working: In water, dimethylamine is the strongest base. Inductive donation, H-bonded solvation of the cation and steric effects balance best for the 2° amine. Aniline is weakest because its lone pair is delocalised into the ring. NH3 and CH3NH2 lie in between.

neet_che_u18_t02_2.working: For ethyl amines in water, the combined inductive, solvation and steric effects give the order 2° > 3° > 1° > NH3: Et2NH > Et3N > EtNH2 > NH3.

neet_che_u18_t02_3.working: Increasing pKb means decreasing basicity. -OMe (+R) donates more than -CH3 (+I/hyperconjugation), and -NO2 (-R) withdraws. Approximate pKb values: anisidine 8.7 < toluidine 8.9 < aniline 9.4 < p-nitroaniline ~13.

neet_che_u18_t02_4.working: In benzylamine the CH2 group insulates the nitrogen from the ring, so the lone pair is not delocalised. It is therefore more basic than aniline. A is true and R is false.

neet_che_u18_t02_5.working: I: in the gas phase, basicity follows the inductive order 3° > 2°. In water, Me2NH > Me3N because of solvation and steric effects, so I is correct. II: anilinium has pKa about 4.6, methylammonium about 10.6, so anilinium is the stronger acid and II is correct.
